name: Coral Senate
subtitle: Token-weighted DAO
description: Example 11 — hash-committed proposals, off-chain weighted vote signatures (zero state per vote), quorum-checked execution behind a timelock window.
long_description: Minimal governance for a token-weighted community. Proposals commit only the keccak256 hash of the action they intend to execute — full calldata lives off-chain, and execution re-derives and matches the hash. Voting happens off-chain entirely: holders sign the proposal hash and a relayer submits the sorted bundle; recovered addresses are strictly ascending so duplicates and invalid signatures are rejected in one rule. Vote weight is balanceOf at execution time — a documented trade-off that avoids per-account checkpoint state. After the voting period a timelock window gives dissenters time to exit before anyone may execute. Proposals cost two state slots, each vote costs zero, and executions reuse the existing packed slot: participating at scale costs the state of the proposals alone.
